h1: Thickness Measurement for Ships at Figueira da Foz and the Mondego
intro: Figueira da Foz is a river port at the mouth of the Mondego on Portugal's Atlantic coast. Ships come here for forest products from the surrounding region, for cement and other bulk, and for repair at a local shipyard. The port is small, with a bar and limited depths, so gauging fits berth stays and yard periods. Atlantis NDT mobilises technicians from India to join the vessel.

highlights.p: Ships loading wood pulp, paper and other forest products bring clean, large holds and deck areas. Between cargoes, empty holds allow thorough gauging of tank tops, frames and bulkheads.
A shipyard on the Mondego repairs coasters, fishing vessels and workboats, so shell, sea chest and rudder gauging can be tied to a docking and the attending surveyor's visit.
The Mondego bar can be closed by Atlantic swell, and depths limit which ships come in. We hold flexible dates so weather delays do not waste the technicians' travel.

port.h: Figueira da Foz and the Mondego estuary
p: Figueira da Foz lies on the central Portuguese coast, where the Mondego river meets the Atlantic. The commercial port is on the river's north bank, upstream of a long breakwater and behind a bar that can be dangerous in heavy swell. Dredged channels give access to the quays, but depths are limited, so the port takes small and medium-sized ships. In winter storms the entrance can close for periods, and arrivals shift accordingly. The town itself is a seaside resort, and the commercial port sits beside the beaches and the fishing harbour.

Traffic is dominated by the forest industry. Pulp and paper mills in the region ship products through Figueira, and the port also handles cement, aggregates, fertiliser, cereals and other bulk cargoes. General cargo and break-bulk coasters complete the mix, and the fishing harbour keeps a fleet of trawlers and smaller boats busy. Tugs and pilot boats assist ships through the entrance. Container traffic is small and the port does not receive large cruise ships, so its customers are mainly short-sea and coastal operators.

Planning at Figueira follows the river. Ships plan arrivals around the tide and the swell forecast at the bar, and pilots decide when movement is safe. Once alongside, a loading or discharge stay may last several days, which suits gauging of holds and deck areas when the ship is empty. A docking at the local yard is a longer opportunity, especially for fishing vessels and coasters that need class surveys. Our approach is to set a flexible start date, confirm access with the agent, and keep the scope tight enough to finish if a delay shortens the stay.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done at Figueira da Foz
p: The port has a shipyard on the Mondego, the Estaleiro Naval do Mondego, which handles repair and conversion of coasters, fishing vessels and workboats. A ship docked or hauled out there can have its shell plating, sea chests, rudder and propeller areas measured, and the yard's staging and access are arranged through the yard planner. Ships too big for the yard go to other Portuguese or Galician yards, and Figueira then provides the afloat gauging ahead of the move.

At the cargo quays, holds on bulk carriers and coasters can be gauged once cargo is discharged, holds are cleaned and the crew declares them safe. Ballast tanks and voids are gauged when emptied and ventilated. Forest-products carriers, which tend to have large clear holds, are straightforward to inspect after a clean discharge. Fishing vessels at the fishing harbour are gauged afloat for owners who want a condition record ahead of a survey or sale. Access to each location is arranged through the ship's agent, and every compartment is entered under the ship's own entry permit.
list: Cargo quays on the Mondego — hold, coaming and tank-top gauging on pulp, paper, cement and bulk ships after discharge.
Shipyard on the river — shell, sea chest, rudder and propeller-area gauging during dockings.
Fishing harbour — hull and tank gauging on trawlers ahead of surveys or sales.
Lay-by berths — condition gauging of idle coasters before charter or sale.
Ballast tanks and voids — gauged afloat once emptied, ventilated and released by the crew.
Pre-docking calls — afloat readings feeding steel estimates for yards in Figueira, Aveiro or Galicia.

context.h: Port state control and rules at Figueira da Foz
p: Portugal is part of the Paris MoU, and port state control at Figueira da Foz follows the regional risk-based system. Inspections are carried out under the Directorate-General for Natural Resources, Safety and Maritime Services, known as DGRM, with the local harbour master responsible for port administration. Older coasters and bulk carriers with a history of wastage are inspected more often, so a recent gauging report helps the superintendent see in advance where an inspector is likely to focus.

EU rules play a role too. Shipping is within the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime applies, though the coastal ships that visit Figueira da Foz may fall below the tonnage thresholds for some obligations. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships in EU ports, and thickness gauging is often arranged alongside that update. For most customers here the real driver is the class survey cycle, or the decision whether to renew steel or retire an ageing hull. Fishing vessels follow separate flag-state and class rules, and we scope them to match.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Figueira da Foz
jobs.p: Jobs here are small-ship work shaped by the river. The superintendent or owner provides the last gauging record, the survey due date and the expected berth or yard period, and we agree the spaces to be covered. Typical requests:
list: Hold, coaming and tank-top plating gauging on a paper or pulp carrier after discharge, for an intermediate or renewal survey.
Shell plating, sea chest and rudder-area gauging on a coaster at the Mondego shipyard, with readings shared with the class surveyor.
Ballast-tank and deck gauging on a bulk coaster at the cement or bulk quay.
Condition gauging of a trawler's hull and tanks before a survey or a sale.
Re-gauging of renewed plating after yard repair, to confirm that fitted steel matches drawing thickness.

logistics: Porto's Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport is the main international arrival point, with Lisbon as an alternative; both are reachable by road. Technicians from India connect through a European hub. The ship's agent arranges port and yard access and any launch. Portugal is a Schengen state, so Schengen visas are obtained in India before departure, and the application begins once the arrival or docking date is firm and the owner has provided an invitation letter naming the vessel. Bar closures can move dates, so travel is confirmed against the agent's latest information.

faqs.q: Is there a shipyard at Figueira da Foz?
faqs.a: Yes, a shipyard on the Mondego repairs coasters, fishing vessels and workboats, and it is where shell gauging out of the water is realistic. Ships beyond its size dock elsewhere. We check with the owner whether the vessel fits the yard before planning a mobilisation.

faqs.q: What happens if the Mondego bar is closed?
faqs.a: The ship waits offshore or at a nearby port until pilots judge the entrance safe. We hold a flexible start date and confirm with the agent before travel. If the delay is long, the job moves to the new arrival date rather than being squeezed into a shorter stay.

faqs.q: Can holds on a paper or pulp carrier be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, after discharge, once holds are cleaned and declared safe. We measure tank tops, lower frames, bulkheads and coamings, comparing readings with the ship's thickness records. Clean holds are usually straightforward, though residue on plating is swept away first so that readings are taken on bare steel.

faqs.q: Do you gauge fishing vessels at Figueira da Foz?
faqs.a: Yes. Hull plating, fish-hold structure, tank boundaries and deck areas can be gauged afloat or at the yard. Owners usually request it before a survey or sale, and we report by compartment so the buyer, the class surveyor or the yard can use the same record.
